title: The six labels: one language for writing and markup
description: Item 20 of 23 Nov 2026, set in stone. Each label: what it covers, where the fix goes, and your own past comments as examples.
intro: One language for both of us, used at every point of the loop: before drafting, in the rules, in your markup, and in what gets stored.
Built from two models: Richards (what is said, feeling, tone, intention) and Flower and Hayes (planning, putting into words, reviewing). The examples are your own comments, word for word.
Cards 1 to 6 are proposed definitions. Cards 13 to 17 are your calls, with no pick from Claude.

sections.title: The six labels
sections.sub: Proposed definitions. Go, or say what to change.

cards.title: Content: what is said
rows: Facts, events, quotes, built details, research. Material that is wrong, missing, or not in your records.
How a true fact is phrased. That is wording.
The brain and the fact sheet
"where the fuck did healthy come from?" and "he would tally the count, then it goes back to zero"

cards.title: Structure: where things go
rows: Order, joins between lines and paragraphs, repeats, gaps, what sits in which section, headings, the length of a part.
What a part is for. That is intention.
The outline and the review file
"this point seems to be repeated too much" and "did I just miss several paragraphs"

cards.title: Intention: what a part is for
rows: The point of a passage, what the reader should get or do, whether a part earns its place, building up to an exercise.
How it sounds. That is tone.
The blank and the section line
"If this is an exercise I will give, or a flagship part of the framework, I want to allude to it and build hype to it."

cards.title: Tone: how you come across to the reader
rows: Your attitude to the reader: warm, sure, beside them, know-it-all, preachy, pitying, cold, transactional.
One word choice, unless that word changes how you come across.
The section line and the tone bank
"I don't like the advice and diagnosis and knowitallness" and "session feels transactional. I want to make it feel like I am a great coach, while being a warm interaction."

cards.title: Wording: how it is put into words
rows: Word choice, how a sentence is built, choppy lines, fragments, vague images, slop, plain words, parallels.
Grammar and punctuation. That is mechanics.
Keeper lines. A rule only when you name a lesson.
"slop?", "what is this vague metaphor no one ever uses?" and "also these are choppy."

cards.title: Mechanics: grammar and marks
rows: Anything that changes your wording or your tense on purpose.
"oxford comma important" and "the and you should be parallel. either both thes or both you(r)ss"

cards.title: Feeling (how you feel about the subject: amused, serious, sad): its own label, or part of tone?

sections.title: How the labels are used
sections.sub: Proposed. Go, or say what to change.

cards.title: One comment can carry more than one label
rows: Claude splits the comment, and each part goes to its own fix.
"too blocky. No warmth." is wording (blocky) and tone (warmth).

cards.title: Praise gets a label too
rows: A line you praise gets the label of what you praised, and is kept as a good example in the right store.
"good edit. I like this style of self conversation" is tone, and goes to the tone bank.

cards.title: A comment with no clear label
rows: Claude labels it from the passage it sits on, and marks it (guess).

cards.title: Your codes: how short?
cards.context: A code in a comment overrides Claude's label, the same way /privileged works today.

cards.title: Where the labels live
rows: In the brain, one row per label, as the single copy. The writer skill reads them from there when drafting and when reading your markup. No copy in a doc, a skill or memory.
Your rule: a second copy drifts.

sections.title: Where the labels touch
sections.sub: Your past words that sit on a boundary. Your call on each. Claude has no pick.

cards.title: A comment is a note on its passage, not a rule
cards.context: Settled by your words of 6 Oct ("others feel like overfitting", when rules were proposed from single comments) and 30 Oct ("that is my observation about how the ai writes, not a command"). A label never turns a comment into a rule. A rule still goes through propose-language-rule, on your go.
